subject: arts-music
unit_title: Portfolio and Public or Private Exhibition

rubric.exceeds: Every step, value, or rendered choice is accurate and faithful to the stated criteria, with no notable errors.
rubric.meets: The work is accurate and faithful to the stated criteria, with at most one minor self-correctable error.
rubric.developing: The work is mostly accurate but has one or more errors that change the result or the intended effect.
rubric.beginning: Multiple accuracy or fidelity errors prevent the work from meeting the stated criteria.

rubric.exceeds: Every claim or choice is backed by specific evidence or clearly explained reasoning a reader can follow unaided.
rubric.meets: Most claims or choices are backed by evidence or reasoning, with only small gaps.
rubric.developing: Some claims are supported but several are asserted without support.
rubric.beginning: Claims are asserted with little or no supporting evidence or reasoning.

rubric.exceeds: The record shows the actual working order, including abandoned attempts and dead ends, in enough detail to reconstruct the session.
rubric.meets: The required log, trace, or notes are present and record what was done and why.
rubric.developing: Documentation exists but is thin, out of order, or written after the fact from memory.
rubric.beginning: Little or no record of the process was kept.

scoring_judgment_guidance: Score this session with the rubric below, not against a fixed answer key — a creative or analytical task legitimately has more than one valid solution. Score only what a guided practice (first pass) on artist statements can show: this is one increment of progress, so score the increment and its documentation rather than the unfinished whole. Record the level reached on each dimension with one specific reason drawn from the actual submission. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about artist statements.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about artist statements; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use sketch or rehearsal record, created or performed work, artist statement, critique, revision, and portfolio reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence/reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

unit_assessment_reference.note: This lesson is one session inside the unit; the unit assessment record above is the summative instrument, and this lesson rubric scores only this session's evidence.

remediation_plan: Reteaching for artist statements follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for artist statements, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for artist statements works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of artist statements, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking artist statements mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension_plan: Apply artist statements under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on artist statements rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.

safety_and_privacy.note: No public performance, camera, voice recording, photograph, or audience is required at any point; a private option and a written/no-audio alternative are stated in the task package and score identically.
